steps.title: Open images in Fiji
steps.instruction: Launch Fiji (ImageJ) and open the immunofluorescence (IF) images containing the two fluorescent channels to be analyzed.

steps.title: Run JaCoP to calculate PCC
steps.instruction: In Fiji, select the Just Another Co-localization Plugin (JaCoP) and run it on each image to compute Pearson’s correlation coefficient (PCC) between the two channels.

steps.title: Compute and interpret PCC values
steps.instruction: Ensure JaCoP calculates PCC across all pixels of each image; note that a PCC near +1 indicates strong positive co‑localization, near 0 indicates random distribution, and near –1 indicates anti‑correlation.

steps.title: Plot and statistically evaluate PCC
steps.instruction: Export the PCC values, plot them, and perform statistical analysis using GraphPad Prism software.
